Instruction to the candidates for Medical Examination CSE PT 2024

Important things for CSE Interview D-day:

1. e-Summon letter

2. Few passport size photos (3-6) - mandatory 2 photos for interview, (10 for medical)

3. Photo ID card (as mentioned in e summon letter)

4. 10th certificate/marksheet original

5. Graduation degree / provisional degree / 8th sem summary marksheet + rest semester marksheet just for reference purpose - original
(Post grad degree if required)

6. Caste /EWS /PwD certificate

7. One set of self attested documents ( if possible take another spare set also) 

8. Affidavit-(In case there is discrepancy- if any, check your mail for the same, upsc must have communicated to you if any undertaking or Affidavits is needed)

9. T.A. bills related stuff if you are claiming it like Flight tickets etc


10. Do not panic if you have missed on some of the documents or if some issue have been raised by the document examiner/UPSC deligate with your documents. Remember this is a preliminary document verification only, you will get ample time for required original documents submission. 
Focus more on the essential i.e. the interview.

Mobile phones / bag etc will be duly submitted/placed in safe custody at the UPSC bhawan so don't worry about it. You can keep your diary with you in Circular Hall.  


Lastly,

Do bring your 3Cs with you ie CONFIDENCE, CALMNESS AND COMMON SENSE before entering into Dholpur House. It's the last leap in this CSE cycle but not the last of your life. Treat it like that only. Give your best and leave rest to GOD.

Name - Polar Bear
Interview Date - 7 Jan
Board- Shri BB Swain Sir
DAF Keywords- Meerut, IIT Bombay, ECE, Cricket, kabbadi, NCC, Paper of AI and ML, Following world affairs

Chairman Sir
Congratulated me on reaching interview stage. then asked

- How you are feeling today? Asked me whether you are happy or disappointed that your interview is on 1st day.
- Directly said about whats happening in cricket now a days apart form the game. (he was hinting about Rohit Sharma PR issue).
- Out of cricket and kabbadi, which one you like most ? Why?
- History of kabbadi and mahabharat relation? few technical specifications and rules?
- if you have to change one rule o cricket? 
- maximum run a player can score in an over ? 
(here i was thinking of jhethalal answer of scoring 50 runs 😅)
- India should reconsider its decision not to play cricket in Pakistan for the Champions Trophy ? Possible implications?
- Few counter questions but seems satisfied with my answers

Member 1:
- about women in constituent assembly ?
- corruption in judiciary ? Any law in place to address this ?
- New Zealand parliament performed a haka to protest a controversial bill? Bill is about? Community name ?
- classical language new ones ? schedule 8 related question
- Bangladesh crisis and  what india should do now ? 
- Recent south korea crisis ? possible implications? role of north korea

Member 2:

- NCC me kya sikha ? Don't you think it should be made compulsory?
- Question on semiconductor ? How i organised that semianar?
How i arranged that much fund  and follow up questions ?
- India target in electronic manufacturing ? And current status? Is india lagging behind?
Why china is world leader in this ? What india can learn ? India loosing ground etc
- Questions of spectrum auctioning ?
- Tell me about any most memorable moment of your iit days?


Member 3:

- AI vs ML ? Use of AI in Warfare? 
- Content of my paper published (AI) (Seems very interested in this topic. asked multiple questions on this)
- what is LLMs ? Don't the posses threat to individual security ?
- Is it possible  to train them emotionally ? 

Member 4:

- Have you ever attended mahakumbh?
- How up govt using AI to manage crowd in mahakumbh?
- Question on India-Canada diplomatic relation?
- Asked me to name european country where india have visa-free access?
-Question on recent UP investor summit and Meerut developmet prospect

Member 2
- Question in Fit India Movement.
- Then why actors/cricketer moving towards politics ? 


The board was very cordial. Giving me ample time to think and respond, even giving me cues and encouraging me like "ha aur socho". Extremely opposite of any mock interviews.
I would say my interview is mostly based on DAF. Although some questions seems like current affairs based but since world affairs keyword is in my Daf so i consider those questions related to my daf only.


**Mock Interview - Don't have much time so took only 3 mock - Samkalp, Chankya & Vajiram. i would suggest to give atleast 3 mock to get the hold of interview. Mocks were mainly helpful for non-verbal cues. Content wise i don't feel that mock will help you much because some mocks were too factual for me and some were very  generic.


**One to One Session with Rahul Sir (IAS PCS Pathshala). 
He spent almost 2 hours with me. His insights were excellent on how to answer questions and generate point  and manage situations when you don't know the answer. 
Since my interview is mainly daf based his daf discussion in detail and provided potential interview questions on extracurricular activities were incredibly helpful for brainstorming different dimensions. 
I highly recommend everyone to have at least one session with him.

Lastly I would like to thank this community for their continuous support and valuable transcripts.🙏

Chemist
DAF details – Chemistry (grad + post grad), DU college, IIT X, Women empowerment, reading about new and emerging energy sources, other keywords – no questions
Board – Dr. Dinesh Dasa (second to go – forenoon session)
Chairman –
Aap Hindi m comfortable hain baat karne m... I said my medium is English. He said koi baat nahi ap ye chorho bahar jo hawa banti hai ki Hindi medium walo ko marks nhi milte esa kch nhi hai… ap btao apko kis language m baat karni hai. I said sir I am comfortable in English. He said okay, let’s start.
1. Sitting on this chair is a dream for many. So, how are you feeling today?
2. Tell me famous personalities from your college (UG/ PG both)
3. Govt. is investing so much in IITs, but IITians go abroad, leading to complete waste of money. What is your view on this?
4. But IITians don’t make up even 1% of ISRO scientists and other leading bodies… what exactly is then their contribution in India?
5. If you are asked to choose between One Nation One Election and Women Reservation Bill (recent one), which one will you choose and why?
(I said women reservation – because we have proof that it’s working – in local bodies)
counter question – but there is issue of Pradhan Pati in local bodies, isn’t it?
6. You study about energy sources, tell me total installed capacity of India and the % share of each source. (I was not sure, so said >60% coal, and others are within 40% - woman member said but you didn’t tell hydro – chairman intervened saying that she said 40% is rest)
7. You have done Chemistry – what has Indian PM committed regarding chemicals in COP 21 & COP 26? (No idea- just mentioned our INDCs)
Member 1 -
1. What is Green Hydrogen? What are the issues in its adoption and what can govt. do about it?
2. Is there any innovative way to tackle the transportation/ logistics issue associated with it?
3. How much expensive is it when compared to Black hydrogen?
4. Do you know REACH scheme? (No idea)
5. What potential applications do you see in green H2?
Member 2 –
1. You come from Delhi-NCR, what policy solutions do you offer for its pollution problem? Do you think discouraging private vehicles can be a good option?
2. Okay, so should we opt for measures like imposing congestion fees during peak hours?
Member 3 –
1. You won essay on women empowerment, what was the exact topic and what did you write in it?
2. Don’t you think looking at present circumstances; we have failed in women empowerment?
3. Recently, the Union Cabinet approved 3 things regarding farmers. What were they? ( I mentioned Agri Marketing policy, but he said no no.. one was PM FBY, tell me the other.. I said yes sir extension of DAP subsidy..)
4. So, what is the reason for doing it? 
Member 4 (lady member) –
1. Continuing with the discussion on women empowerment, tell me your interpretation of this statement – ‘ We have started to raise our daughters as 21st century women, but continue to raise boys in the 19th century.’
2. (I said there are both sides to it etc.) You are playing safe here, I think there are more men who are restricting women r/t supporting. So, do you think supporting men will increase in future?
3. Do you know about the chemical weapons convention? 
4. Okay, so we didn’t ask anything on IR. Recently, the Canadian PM has offered his resignation. How do you see this development in India-Canada relations?
Chairman –
1. Okay, so how do you think the regime in a country, example in US now the Republicans will come to power, affects its relations with India? (I said foreign policy driven by national interests in long run, but political leadership may lead to minor modifications)
2. So, do you think Canada strained relations with India in national interest or because of political reasons?
Member 2 – 
(Smiling) Do you have foreign service as your preference? (I think the context of this question was chairman sir’s remarks on my Canada answer- he smilingly said very good answer – not sure if it was a taunt or genuine comment)
Chairman – okay, thank you.
Overall experience –
Very cordial board.

Q.12 How it protect farmer?-> by setting a minimum price, the market price goes up
Q.13 Why are farmers protesting?-> msp legalisation

Q.15 What is the solution then? -> land consolidation, agri infra, exposure to contract farming, rural industrialisation, remove disguised unemployment, real rural wage growth increase
Q.16 How is Trump going to affect India?-> I said it has both positive and negative way
Positive: focus shift on China from Russia, Boost to Quad, Indo Pacific policy, oppurtunity for Indian market like heavy truck industry
Negative: Tariff, Trade, Trump will ask some tougher questions, Reduction of tariff on Electric vehicles, angle of Elon Musk
In all the ans she felt a bit unsatisfied, but when I was answering other members' questions then she nodded her head with full energy, I felt like she was happy with my ans, but not when I was answering her questions, more than half of interview was taken by her only, tried to grill me a little bit. When I was answering to her, other members were noting something on paper

Member 2: Very simple, old man
Q.1 What has IIT contributed? They all go abroad, and waste govt resources. I said to some extent, yes brain drain is there, Covid-> Ambu bags, cheap ventilator, IIT Bombay-> 1st CAR T cell therapy, IIT Madras -> BANDICOOT robot
Q.2 Three laws, Hindi name, why it has been introduced?-> BNS, BNSS
Home minister-> ANTI colonialism, accept Technological evidence, define organised crime, so with changing society we needed them
Q.3 Who is your role model and why? I said my father-> doctor, his dedication to public service imbibed the spirit of public service in me.
Q.4 Ok Nihal, just one last question, Despite technological measures why we can’t reduce crime? Can we dream of a crime-free society? I said we can dream of crime-free society, but it must be matched with actions-> Integrated criminal judicial reform, speedy justice, more infrastructure, Prison reform-> retributive to reformative justice

Member 3: bit young
Q.1 Since maths is optional, Tell me about the prize given in the field of mathematics which is comparable to the Noble Prize. -> Abels prize, Norwegian govt, Field medal prize

Q.2 Any prize in India-> Ramanujan Price
Q.3 Any Indian who got both prizes?-> I said Manju Bhargava got the Field medal, but not sure about Ramanujan's price-> He said he got both, rule of 30-40 years and other stuff, I said thank you for the information, sir,
Q.4 What is an Energy Audit, any scheme where it is useful? I said input, output, and how much percentage is sourced from renewable energy, can be used as an incentive to reduce energy demand. Perform Achieve Trade scheme
Q.5 What is happening in Manipur, Kuki-Metei conflict-> I said development gap, proximity to border

Member 4 Full-on grilling mode
Q.1 Do an energy audit of this building? What thins you will look?
I said demand, supply, wastage of energy
Q.2 Don’t you look for various load values? What are they?
I said don’t remember exact load of appliances
Q.3 He said what are appliances being used? I said Heater, light
Then he said pump also for water
Q.4 Let's suppose you did an energy audit, how will you reduce energy demand?
I said to paint the building with heat absorbent, which reduces heat load, then I said the Internet of things, connecting devices-> auto cut, I felt he was looking for more practical solution while my ans was idealistic
Q.5 Have you heard of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency? I said appliance rating
Q.6 Can’t you see AC, I said yes it’s 2-star, we should switch to 5-star
Then he said CFL bulb, I said yes sir energy efficient appliances should be used
This was the section of the interview where I felt embarrassed, he even said you are an engineer that's why we are asking you these things
Q.7 What is carbon trading when was it introduced by whom? I told everything 1 tonn certificate, UNFCCC, Kyoto protocol, Regulation under Baku declaration
Q.8 view on liquor ban policy in Bihar, they are foregoing 20,000 cr annually
I said it has also led to a reduction in crime, domestic violence, road accident
However, we have  tourism opportunities so middle path-> Hotel mein bech sakte hai, easy grant of permission to tourists like Gujarat govt
He further asked I said our state is a welfare state, I see it as a pure means to achieve the right ends
Q.9 Let us suppose you are the Finance secretary of Bihar-> then you will ans the same thing, here chairman started laughing saying there can be no ans to this question.
Then they said your interview is over, I thanked them all and went out

The start of my interview was a bit unconventional but then it gained momentum. The board members seemed very interested in my answers. It felt more like a discussion rather than a traditional question answer session.

Mock Interview - Since this my 4th interview. So i attended only 2 mock interview - Samkalp and Chahal. 
Based on my experience I can say that if it is your first interview you should give at least 5-6 interviews to boost your confidence. Otherwise 2-3 interviews are sufficient.

One to One - I attended more 121 than mock interview. 
121 with 
- Satyam Jain - Avoid this.
- Ravindran Sir - Recommended. Discussed variety of question and it will  help you.
- Rahul Sir (ias pcs pathshala) - Highly Recommended. Very much beneficial for structuring and concluding the answer. Sir value addition part was extremely enriching.
- Dharmadhikari Sir - Recommended. Very helpful in confidence boosting.

In a real interview, questions from mock sessions and onetoone discussions will not get repeated but the approach you develop will help you answer random questions. (However I got a bit lucky as 3 questions I had discussed with Rahul Sir were repeated - caste census wala, Bihar-  Jharkhand, and sports section wala🙂)


I believe you should try to articulate your answers in an engaging manner. Avoid giving just 1-2 line responses. Show enthusiasm and eagerness in every answer. Try to cover multiple perspectives using succinct keywords. 

Lastly all the best to everyone and thanking this channel for providing transcript. It was very much helpful 🙏

1. Growth in Top Scorers (200+):

 2.9% (2021) → 3.7% (2022) → 4.4% (2023), reflecting improved high-end performance.  

2. Decline in Mid-Tier Scores (170-189): 
   - Both 170-179 and 180-189 ranges saw consistent declines:  
     - 170-179: 29.2% → 25.18% → 24.11%  
     - 180-189: 20.44% → 17.69% → 17.23% 
   - Suggests a shift toward higher or lower score brackets.  

3. Lowest Score Range (<150):  
   - Dropped sharply from 10.95% (2021) to 7.2% (2022) but slightly rose to 7.9% (2023). May indicate fluctuating performance among lower-scoring candidates.  

4. Stabilization in 190-200 Range:  
   - After a dip from 13.14% (2021) to 11.26% (2022), it stabilized at 11.32% (2023).  


5. 160-169 Range Rebound:  
   - After a dip in 2022 (21.98%), this range slightly recovered to 22.15% (2023), hinting at possible variability in mid-tier performance.  

Conclusion: Scores are polarizing, with more candidates achieving top marks (200+) and fewer in mid-tiers (170-189). The lowest tier (<150) remains volatile but smaller than in 2021.

✅ One on One - Rahul Sir of IAS PCS PATHSHALA and Dharmadhikari Sir.
I deeply thank both of them especially rahul sir for his input on articulation of answer and explaining the nitty gritty of answering🙏

To sum up the experience i would say although it is called a personality test..you need to be well prepared for it. The panel will have 30 minutes to judge your personality and in the same way  you will also have those 30 minutes to showcase the aspects of your personality that work in your favor.

✅ Important Note: Prepare your DAF very well. I went through many transcripts and noticed that no questions related to IRS or the budget were being asked. However Rahul Sir advised me to prepare them since they were part of my DAF and eventually questions from those areas did come up in my interview. So the bare minimum you can do is to prepare your DAF well...focus on what is in your control. Control the controllable.

Overall experience : it was completely unrelated to mocks. Nothing based on Current affairs. Round big (dinner)table like setup not seen any where in mocks. More of discussion than QnA. 4/5 members grilled continuously to see if would I change my stance
 1. Chair person 
 a. Long discussion on how customary practices are being increasingly becoming uniform due to modern law. It was at this point I said I don’t know and he said let me finish. This is not QnA, we will have Intelligent discussion. I apologised and let him continue 
 b.  Do you think such modern laws that brings uniformity in customs is necessary ?
 c. How do we resolve such disputes ?
 d. Have you heard of streedhan? 
 e. Can SC be involved in this ? 
 f. Do you know of hindu succession act? And discussion on how bringing uniformity in law is causing troubles in such aspects?
 2. Member 1 
 a. Talked about NEET (30% youth not in education, employment or training). How do we solve this? 
 b. Why govt is not able to provide this? 
 c.  he said people are shifting from one job to another, what could be the reasons ? 
 d. I mentioned something about state govt, he asked why state govts are not able to provide ? 
 e. Follow up on my answer, what is the use of freebies, your take on it? I gave my opinion and said there should be sunset clause to the end. He asked how many years 3 or 4 or 5 or 10 years? I said that should be done based on Cost benefit ratio and party consensus
 f. Discussion on capital expenditure and revenue expenditure, should we have more capex?
 g. All along this while, the chairman continuously rang bell for puine, went out multiple times to see if would be distracted. no matter what, I did not even care for such actions. Just focused on the person I was answering 
 3. Member 2 (very close to my left) 
 a. Greeted hello X, continuing on chairperson discussion, you say there should be balance or should communities themselves resolve this? I said if constitutional aspect of dignity is violated state should intervene, else communities can themselves resolve other matters 
 b. What is your take on Cock fighting that happens during festivals in AP ? Even MPs/MLAs are known to be involved in this, can communities involve in such issues? I said since betting is involved govt should get involved. He then said, remove the gambling aspect, can communities resolve any other issues amongst themselves or should we ban such practices, say even jallikatu? 
 c. How to resolve the issue of stray dogs ? I said stakeholder approach and was continuing, to which he immediately abrupted and said don’t use fancy words, if you are adminstrator what would you do ? 
 d. Since you watch movies, do you justify allu arjun arrest. Was he truly responsible for the stampede? 
 e. In the past too such events happened, can we still arrest them even now? 
 4. Member 3 (close to my right) -she is such a sweet heart. 
 a. Given difference in location of your studies, how different was your school and IIT life especially interms of academics, infra and education? 
 b. What all would you change in your education system, especially in the school you have studied? 
 c. Some discussion on NEP and can it be successful ? 
 d. What is the role of local administration in ensuring the administration of school. I asked if it just the role of MLAs? She said all local administration, to which I gave suited response? 
 e. Role of AI in education? Can it help? 
 f. Isn't there excessive focus on Maths (STEM), what was your experience in school? What should be the focus in future ? 
 5. Member 4 (Had very difficult time in understanding his pronunciations) 
 a. Have you heard about QUAD? 
 b. Is it military alliance? Do you think its Anti china?  (he was pushing me to say it was a military anti china block)
 c. Is it fulfilling its mandate?

(2/2)
d. Given all the global instability, If we go against war with china in indopacific will the neighbours in indopacific come to our rescue? 
 e. Based on my response, he asked what is NAM? Why did we adopt such a philosophy? What is our current policy? 
 f. While our neighbours have elected women as PMs or presidents, india has not been able to do so? What is your take? 
 
Chairman said your interview is over, I thanked everyone and left the place. 
 
All in all, it was a completely different ball game. I went into the place thinking its just another day. This helped me keep my calm. But truth to be told, my heart raced when I was being called to the room. So maintain your calm, don’t get distracted, what people say in mock interviews is not completely relavant.

4 one to one dicussions with : sangamitra maam from Hyderabad, KSG (khan sir), pranay aggrawal sir for sociology and Mridul sir (overall discussions). In my opinion one to one DISCUSSIONS are more better than these artificial panel mocks. Do give 2 of them to be confident or getting used to answering 4-5 elders.

Overall experience: Extremely cordial and polite board, gave me ample time to answer despite me being the last candidate for the day, almost entirely opinion/analysis questions (didn't have to say "I don't know" for anything), full board was smiling throughout and 2-3 times when I said something funny all 5 members laughed together, felt more conversational than any mock I'd taken.

It felt different from mocks. Honestly, the mocks seemed much more formal than this. The entire board and especially Dasa sir seemed to be in the mood for a relaxed, casual conversation. Idk how they manage to do it, but they know how to make you feel super comfortable and relaxed. It seemed almost perfectly designed to bring out our honest opinions and thoughts. The closest experience like this was at Samkalp.

Very sincerely, thank you to everyone who shared their transcripts here. A few questions were repeated by Dasa sir. Reading transcripts was very helpful.

All the very best to everyone appearing ! ❤️

IPS vacancies Distribution 
Batch 2023 & 2024

The major differences in IPS vacancy distribution between batch 2023 and 2024 are as follows:  

 1. State/Cadre-wise Total Vacancy Changes 
- Significant Increases:  
  - Bihar: 2 → 15 (+13)  
  - Karnataka: 5 → 9 (+4)  
  - Maharashtra: 12 → 16 (+4)  
  - Manipur: 8 → 16 (+8)  
  - Madhya Pradesh: 10 → 13 (+3)  

- Significant Decreases:  
  - West Bengal: 23 → 9 (−14)  
  - Telangana: 6 → 1 (−5)  
  - Tripura: 5 → 1 (−4)  
  - Gujarat: 10 → 5 (−5)  
  - Assam Meghalaya: 8 → 5 (−3)  
  - Uttar Pradesh: 28 → 20 (−8)  

---

2. Category-wise Trends 
- OBC Vacancies: Increased from 53 (2023) to 65 (2024) (+12).  
- UR (Including EWS): Slight decrease from 103 (2023) to 100 (2024) (−3), but Insider UR vacancies rose from 22 to 25.  
- SC/ST: Minimal changes (SC: 31 → 32; ST: 13 → 13).  

---

3. Insider-Outsider Shifts 
- Total Insider Vacancies: Increased from 64 (2023) to 68 (2024).  
- Total Outsider Vacancies: Decreased from 136 (2023) to 132 (2024).  

---

4. Notable State-specific Category Shifts 
- Bihar: Shift from SC/ST vacancies in 2023 (SC=1, ST=1) to UR/OBC dominance in 2024 (UR=6, OBC=7).  
- West Bengal: UR vacancies dropped sharply from 14 to 3.  
- Telangana: All categories reduced, leaving only 1 OBC vacancy.  

---

Summary 
The 2024 vacancy distribution reflects a reallocation favoring states like Bihar, Manipur, and Maharashtra, with a focus on increasing OBC representation and Insider vacancies. Conversely, states like West Bengal, Telangana, and Gujarat saw significant reductions in total vacancies.

Beware of frauds disguising themselves as student saviours and defrauding them of their time, money and mental peace. Make informed choice from multiple credible sources, especially new aspirants! Stay away from people who do not take criticism or ensure credibility for their actions. Ask for marksheets before enrolling in any course. Beware of harmful impacts of AI. Happy learning!

Some statistical modelling done by Krejcie & Morgan and other statisticians suggest that for a sample of around 3000 people, a sample size of around 20%, i.e. data of 600 people is needed for accurate analysis of patterns or behaviours. Hence anyone claiming to know the trend will need data for those many people, otherwise the pattern analysis would be wrong. This much data is not available even to the Chairperson/members or the JS/US, so anyone claiming such trends is just doing creative writing. The level of secrecy and encryption that UPSC is maintaining post some recent events makes it almost next to impossible to get any data leaked, otherwise it would be a blot on the institution. Even if done, it is futile. It is all about the relative performance that matters. Even in optionals, if you have done well, you will get good marks regardless of the subject. You just have to be in the top bracket of that optional.

Similar thing goes with interview. If your interview has gone well, regardless of the board you will get good marks. All boards reward marks in almost the full range(120-200) with the 150-160 bracket being the most crowded, so it is only your performance on that day that matters. So, there is no point getting into the futile discussion as to which board has awarded good marks or which board has not. Just have trust on the outcome. It will be good regardless of what happens in FR-CSM-2024. Just enjoy this time, and keep your calm.

PS: MOST HELPFUL EXERCISE: Group discussions with peers (6 of us, THE BEST thing to do is study in a group for PT)


PPS: MOSTEST HELPFUL EXERCISE: Having one person ask you questions everyday. 25-30 minute slot. Preferably the person should be from CSE preparation. Person must be constructively critical. 




Reason for such a long message: I met a girl at Quantel office who had come to this big city called Delhi first time in her life. She had reached interview stage in her very first attempt. I saw my old self in her, barring the fact that I had much more awareness and much less passion than her in my first attempt. So this detailed message is for every hardworking person out there sitting in a dilapidated room looking at Dholpur House pictures and imagining themselves there- YOU GOT THIS, YOUNGER SISTER/BROTHER. We got you.

Medical process for CSE PT candidates:

On the interview day, you will receive the medical examination letter from UPSC.

The next day, report to the designated hospital with:

Medical examination letter

At least 10 passport-size photographs


At the hospital, you will first be given several forms, including a declaration form (Don't worry about point no.-10, Notice for Medical examination- it has said that "The candidates are required to fill up the declaration form by logging in  cseplus website....."  Declaration form will be provided by designated hospital)  Fill them carefully.

Then the basic check-up will start:

Weight

Height

Chest expansion


After that, you will be sent to different departments:

Surgery (hernia or any past surgery check)

Orthopaedics

Eye

ENT

Medicine (BP and pulse rate)


In the morning itself, the following tests will be done:

Blood sample

Urine sample

Chest X-ray


Once the blood and urine samples are given, you can eat and drink.

After all department-wise examinations are completed, you will receive two attendance slips:

One for your personal record

One to be submitted at the UPSC office


You can submit the attendance slip at UPSC the same day or later.

Also, email a copy of the attendance slip to DoPT.
The email ID is :

[email removed]

That’s it. The medical process is complete.

Important points:

Eye test includes vision and colour blindness (prescription is fine if you have one)

Maintain at least 10 hours of fasting


Note: Medical reports are usually uploaded 25–30 days after the medical examination.

Thank you 🙏

*Sir, in case of a cyber fraud related complaint where the fraud involved multiple bank accounts maintained with multiple banks.

M2: So you mentioned that KYC is done in the banks. Why is it necessary?

M2: Okay so you mentioned about mule accounts. Why are they used?

*Sir, mule accounts acts as the rented bank accounts which are used for illegal transactions involving a fraud or a money laundering.

Name: Murphy's  Law
Date : 3/02/2026, Afternoon. 3rd To go.
Duration: not sure, was waiting for around 5-10 min outside (was called 10 -12 minutes before 3PM), Exit time i saw the clock: 3:35PM 
Board: Had no idea- some ma'am i didn't recognise- as I haven't seen any of their profile,plus couldn't spot any name on cabin before entering- later asked the person who escorted me. 

DAF: Civil Engineering, PSIR, Gaya, Bihar, Jharkhand. Nothing else asked.
Greeted everyone, Ma'am asked me to take my seat.

Ma'am read my DAF and pointed out towards my work experience with an aggregator. 

Ma'am: Are you still working? 
I said no ma'am. (worked till July 2025). 
Ma'am: But you worked for quite sometime here.
I said yes ma'am. 
Ma'am: Is this work related to civil engineering?
I Said no ma'am. It dealt with Time Value of Money. 
She said okay. (i expected a related question as 5 years i did that job)

Ma'am: So, Murphy's Law- Help me understand this. You are a civil engineer, India is a hot climate country yet we have this trend of glass buildings. Why?

(First question itself bouncer for me, given 5+ years gap with Engineering). I couldn't think beyond asthetics.And it wasn't very engineering answer so i didn't said that.
Gave 2 points (1 was horribly wrong)
1. ma'am we also have a lot of dust and it could help in such structures. (realised as soon as those words left my mouth that it was a senseless point). 
ma'am: Dust can be blocked by concrete walls as well. Plus glass gets dirty.
I said Yes ma'am.
2. In some buildings modified glass looking facade is used to act as solar panels as well. 

She nodded , but wasn't fully convinced (as i am sure this wasn't the right explanation)

I then added sorry' ma'am i cannot think of any other engineering justification as of now. (as soon as i saw the first glass building after returning from UPSC bhavan - it struck me; Material costs are key consideration here since steel is more expensive and is integral to modern concrete constructions so glass does offer little glass advantage by limiting use of steel and concrete to just frame)

Ma'am: Okay tell me what are Green buildings.

I said, buildings that are sustainable. Both- during their construction - using low carbon process and materials, as well as during their operations and life cycle.

Ma'am: Tell me some elements of Green buildings. Assuming construction phase has used sustainable process.

I said: 1. Clean air conditioning and heating. 2. Using Footsteps and activities in the building to generate some power. 3. Treating and re-using Grey Water. 
Ma'am interjected and asked- Treated water, meaning rain water harvesting?
I said ma'am Rain water harvesting is a part, but by Grey water -i mean - water from toilets being treated and re used for non drinking purposes like gardening and cleaning.

She seemed convinced.

Ma'am: So you live in Jharkhand. Must have heard about Jamtara. How do we prevent such things if you are posted in any district of Jharkhand?

I said - Ma'am the people involved in Jamtara were mostly footsoldiers. And operated at behest of outside criminal networks  like the ones in south east asia. So awareness will be a key tool in combating.

1. We can make people aware of the same so that they don't fell prey to such criminal networks.
2.Also to make them aware of negative consequences on their life. Being on wrong side of the law can ruin lives as well.
3. Timely detection.I explained using a recent Bihar example where authorities detected a person using Sim Box of 20,000 Sim and defrauded thousands - by tracking abnormal power utilisation.

Ma'am asked how will you spread awareness!?
I said since mostly from rural areas these people are, can take help from local Panchayats- as there is more ground level connect of local leaders to people. 
Also Civil Society organisations. 

(Social media should have been an important part here but didn't even occur to me till i left the room- many such moments will be there throughout the PT)

Ma'am: Okay let's talk about Israel Palestine. Do you see any peace happening there anytime soon?

I started with the India Arab league declaration just a few days ago on the issue reaffirming Palestinian self determination and 2 state solution. And the Gaza peace board. 
Said since the two parties are not on the same page on specifics it's difficult. 
Hamas is reluctant to disarm and Israel reluctant on 2 state solution. 

Ma'am then again asked what do you think? Peace will come here or not?

I Said, ma'am if we look at the history, Very difficult to say peace will occur. Mentioned Camp David accords and Oslo accords. And how something or the other happens. So as things stand peace is not likely.

Ma'am then indicated member to her left.

M1: (Again Civil Engineering related)- Only 2 Qs

Since you are a civil engineer, our country is doing a lot in terms of infrastructure. Is there anything that we have done to streamline coordination in that regard?

I said PM Gatishakti. 
M1: what does it do? 
I said - Inter department and ministerial coordination to minimise delay and facilitate effective execution. 
Pragati portal also i added that helps in fast-track many projects.
He interjected and said Okay okay (probably guessed i know about this :( )

M1: Something about logistics and tracking dashboard for projects. I didn't understand and then he said - where we track projects or something. Do you know about this?
I said No Sir. Sorry. 

He said okay and passed on to next member. 

M3: 
Again started with civil engineering. 
What is this we are doing with river linking? Are you aware?

I said yes sir. The idea is to link water deficit Rivers with water surplus ones via canals to ensure availability of water throughout. 

However it has some issues. 
1. We don't have truly water surplus rivers beyond himalyan rivers. Most are monsoon dependent and these days monsoon is very erratic to give any predictability for water availability. (Can have either excessive rains in short time or just dry spells)

2. The logistical cost is very high. relocation and submergence of large areas (Couldn't remember name of that Tiger reserve which is said to be at risk of submergence and he didn't ask)

Sir nodded. And then asked are there any active projects in river linking? I said - ken betwa river linking, where we are planning to connect surplus ken river with Betwa river to support bundelkhand region.

He nodded again and moved to next topic.

Sir (kind of monologue )- You are native of Bihar. Lets accept it as given that conventional industries won't come to bihar. and leave aside political issues. What could be done? So many bureaucrats come from that state. 

( i was in a spot. without addressing political instability and lack of industries it was difficult to come up with any convincing points)

I said- Sir, predictability and stability are crucial for any investment and industry. And even if we assume no conventional industries are there or Will come, 
Bihar has good potential at MSME level - (i wanted to link SHGs but forgot in midst)- used the example of food processing potential. Talked about Makhana. How Bihar is home to most makhana which is worldwide famous but there is very poor price discovery. Said, we can try to make complete ecosystem here which will be helpful.

Next, as sir mentioned bihar has skilled and talented people, we can explore domains like offering land and skilled manpower for Data centres/Cloud services - for which the budget announced tax holiday till 2047.

Another point i would like to add, is exploring Bihar's huge potential in tourism sector. We have buddhist circuit, Mahabodhi temple etc that can also boost the state.

(Felt Bihar's question could have been answered better but it was like conversation so couldn't just pause and think on templates - somehow felt unnatural)

Sir nodded and moved on to IR.

Do you think India should join Gaza peace board? ( I had mentioned uncertainty of it's role in answer to ma'am's question on Israel Palestine)

I said, we should wait and evaluate if it fits requirements for our core national interest. 
i mentioned -  India is committed towards multilateralism and UN. The board is being proposed as a potential alternative to UN by president Trump. Which goes beyond it's mandate.
Even the P-5 Members; France and UK have declined. So we should wait and see what future this board has.

Sir- okay, do you know what Pax Silica is?
I said - It's a US led grouping of Nations to ensure reduced dependency on Semiconductor and AI technology. 
We have been invited to the grouping soon after the New US ambassador took charge - sir also added this when i mentioned. 

Do you think we should join pax Silica? 

I said Yes. It's in our interest. We have huge dependency on critical elements. mentioned how china had blocked access to rare earths magnets. 
He said - If president Trump says - you can join pax Silica only if you join Gaza peace board. What advice would you tender to the Government of India?

I said,  Pax Silica is in our interest,if they offer us membership without any strings attached i would advise the government to join. 

Sir said - Nothing comes without any strings attached. Other members chuckled in agreement. 

I said - Sir our decision should be guided by our own national interest. If we find the terms not aligned in our favour, we should reconsider joining the pax Silica grouping as well.

Sir said -since the time of Narsimha Rao India has pursued a foreign policy of (something i don't exactly remember , something about not being decisivene)We are an aspiring superpower - is that Narasimha Rao doctrine still valid?don't you think we should be more decisive?

I agreed. and added yes sir decisiveness is indeed very important but we should also have material strength and situation to back up our decision.

I gave example of China which in 1980s and throughout till early 2000s had the luxury of having a supportive America,and they practiced -build your strength and bide your Time. I said we don't have that luxury of that cooperative America at the moment but we should practice the strategy of building strength and bide our time. 

Sir added something more - about that Chinese strategy and said you should read more about this. I said right sir.

So you are a civil engineer (🥲) 

We observe this issues of poor construction quality.  Why is it that we have poor quality compared to British era structures.

I Said - sir one prime reason that i can think of is we follow Project based approach in india. where demand for engineers peak during construction phase. 

On the other hand the idea should be to have life cycle based approach. Where engineers are engaged throughout the life cycle of any structure not just construction. It is followed in developed countries. 
I added NHAI has started doing it. 

Then he started talking about the bridges - Indore, Mumbai and added in Bihar it's common for bridges to fail.

Ma'am: So, Murphy's Law- Help me understand this. You are a civil engineer, India is a hot climate country yet we have this trend of glass buildings. Why?

(First question itself bouncer for me, given 5+ years gap with Engineering). I couldn't think beyond asthetics.And it wasn't very engineering answer so i didn't said that.
Gave 2 points (1 was horribly wrong)
1. ma'am we also have a lot of dust and it could help in such structures. (realised as soon as those words left my mouth that it was a senseless point). 
ma'am: Dust can be blocked by concrete walls as well. Plus glass gets dirty.
I said Yes ma'am.
2. In some buildings modified glass looking facade is used to act as solar panels as well. 

She nodded , but wasn't fully convinced (as i am sure this wasn't the right explanation)

I then added sorry' ma'am i cannot think of any other engineering justification as of now. (as soon as i saw the first glass building after returning from UPSC bhavan - it struck me; Material costs are key consideration here since steel is more expensive and is integral to modern concrete constructions so glass does offer little glass advantage by limiting use of steel and concrete to just frame)

Ma'am: Okay tell me what are Green buildings.

I said, buildings that are sustainable. Both- during their construction - using low carbon process and materials, as well as during their operations and life cycle.

Ma'am: Tell me some elements of Green buildings. Assuming construction phase has used sustainable process.

I said: 1. Clean air conditioning and heating. 2. Using Footsteps and activities in the building to generate some power. 3. Treating and re-using Grey Water. 
Ma'am interjected and asked- Treated water, meaning rain water harvesting?
I said ma'am Rain water harvesting is a part, but by Grey water -i mean - water from toilets being treated and re used for non drinking purposes like gardening and cleaning.

She seemed convinced.

Ma'am: So you live in Jharkhand. Must have heard about Jamtara. How do we prevent such things if you are posted in any district of Jharkhand?

I said - Ma'am the people involved in Jamtara were mostly footsoldiers. And operated at behest of outside criminal networks  like the ones in south east asia. So awareness will be a key tool in combating.

1. We can make people aware of the same so that they don't fell prey to such criminal networks.
2.Also to make them aware of negative consequences on their life. Being on wrong side of the law can ruin lives as well.
3. Timely detection.I explained using a recent Bihar example where authorities detected a person using Sim Box of 20,000 Sim and defrauded thousands - by tracking abnormal power utilisation.

Ma'am asked how will you spread awareness!?
I said since mostly from rural areas these people are, can take help from local Panchayats- as there is more ground level connect of local leaders to people. 
Also Civil Society organisations. 

(Social media should have been an important part here but didn't even occur to me till i left the room- many such moments will be there throughout the PT)

What is this we are doing with river linking? Are you aware?

I said yes sir. The idea is to link water deficit Rivers with water surplus ones via canals to ensure availability of water throughout. 

However it has some issues. 
1. We don't have truly water surplus rivers beyond himalyan rivers. Most are monsoon dependent and these days monsoon is very erratic to give any predictability for water availability. (Can have either excessive rains in short time or just dry spells)

2. The logistical cost is very high. relocation and submergence of large areas (Couldn't remember name of that Tiger reserve which is said to be at risk of submergence and he didn't ask)

Sir nodded. And then asked are there any active projects in river linking? I said - ken betwa river linking, where we are planning to connect surplus ken river with Betwa river to support bundelkhand region.

He nodded again and moved to next topic.

Sir (kind of monologue )- You are native of Bihar. Lets accept it as given that conventional industries won't come to bihar. and leave aside political issues. What could be done? So many bureaucrats come from that state.

How Bihar is home to most makhana which is worldwide famous but there is very poor price discovery. Said, we can try to make complete ecosystem here which will be helpful.

Next, as sir mentioned bihar has skilled and talented people, we can explore domains like offering land and skilled manpower for Data centres/Cloud services - for which the budget announced tax holiday till 2047.

Another point i would like to add, is exploring Bihar's huge potential in tourism sector. We have buddhist circuit, Mahabodhi temple etc that can also boost the state.

i mentioned -  India is committed towards multilateralism and UN. The board is being proposed as a potential alternative to UN by president Trump. Which goes beyond it's mandate.

Sir- okay, do you know what Pax Silica is?

Sir said -since the time of Narsimha Rao India has pursued a foreign policy of (something i don't exactly remember , something about not being decisivene)We are an aspiring superpower - is that Narasimha Rao doctrine still valid?don't you think we should be more decisive?

M4:
So you are a civil engineer (🥲) 

We observe this issues of poor construction quality.  Why is it that we have poor quality compared to British era structures.

I Said - sir one prime reason that i can think of is we follow Project based approach in india. where demand for engineers peak during construction phase. 

On the other hand the idea should be to have life cycle based approach. Where engineers are engaged throughout the life cycle of any structure not just construction. It is followed in developed countries. 
I added NHAI has started doing it. 

Then he started talking about the bridges - Indore, Mumbai and added in Bihar it's common for bridges to fail.

I said - Sir in the context the Bhopal 90degree Bridge (sir said yes Bhopal). Bridges do not get constructed in matter of days. it takes 2-3 years. And there is usually regular audit. It seems it was not properly done otherwise the issue would have been flagged. 

So who do you hold accountable? The contractor would say i am executing the design given. 

I said, sir we need to identify at what levels lapses have been there. Right from design to execution and audit. And need to  fix accountability at every level.

Then again - Why does it happen? 

I said we also have very high tolerance for non compliance in some areas.
(Ma'am raised eyebrows with a grin -and the sir who asked - other members also changed their facial expressions from smiling poker face to wider grin and maybe mild surprise/shock on me uttering those words)

Sir asked- 

North Bihar is flood prone. Are you aware we are constructing a medical College there. 
I said yes sir- AIIMS Darbhanga.

How do you construct in a flood prone area. 

I said- if we have to construct in a water logged situation; can explore coffer dam to halt water and do the foundation work like we do in case of river bridges.

Sir said - Coffer Dam will last only one year or so then what?

I thought he was referring to overall approach towards structures in flood prone areas.
I said we need to have elevated structures on piers or basement having provision for flood waters to pass as is followed in Japan. However for that there needs to be complete interconnectedness of drainage system in the municipality. ( Maybe he wanted to know about identification of areas which are not in flood plain then do the construction but he didn't follow up)

Sir- What is the process to be followed in construction? Do we just do tendering and start??

I said - Sir we start with feasibility study. For example - if we want to construct a road, need to first asess requirement, traffic studies and see if feasible to construct at that area.

Next do preliminary survey. 
(sir said - something related to one step i can't recall but i had said, yes sir it will be part of feasibility studies)
After that design phase and follow up with tendering, then execution.

Glanced at clock while getting up from chair - It was 3:35PM. Had not checked the clock while entering (was zoned out) 

Maybe i entered around 3PM as i was escorted 10 -12 minutes before 3PM from waiting area and waited for 5-10 minutes outside. (Don't know time feels different there)  so I guess around 30 minutes 

Asked the person escorting me back - Kinka board tha. He said with surprise - Suman Sharma Ma'am ka. ( am I cooked 🥲?)

Fumbled a bit in 2-3 places. 
While answering glanced at others occassionally - everyone was listening. Ma'am was noting down stuff here and there. Some members too. 

Felt very different from mocks. Even questions were not in QnA format but just conversation - so couldn't just go with template made answers. Very cordial and comfortable board.

UPSC Interview Transcript

Board: Sheel Vardhan Sir
Date: 12/02/2026- Afternoon

Keywords: Sindhudurg, Maharashtra, Cashew Farming, Kathak, Lavani, Writing Quotes and Poetry, Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering, Sociology, MIT Pune, Magazine Editor, Cultural Club Head

I entered the board and greeted all the members.
---

Chairperson

1. Your name has a connection with ancient literature. Do you know about this?


2. What about the Aranyakas and the Upanishads?


3. You were an editor for a college magazine. Do you read newspapers?


4. I am making a statement. Can you elaborate on this?

“The sports page of a newspaper reflects the full truth, the editorial page reflects half the truth, whereas the front page reflects minimum truth.”

(Some discussion followed.)


5. As your hobby is writing quotes, tell me one quote that guides you.

I said:
“Try to be a rainbow in someone’s cloud.”


6. How would you be a “rainbow” as a District Magistrate?


7. Which scheme, according to you, has the potential to be a rainbow?

I said VB GRAM G — because poverty is the darkest cloud of all, and the scheme provides dignity and meaningful work opportunities.
(He was nodding and appreciating in between.)


8. Define folk dance.

Member 2 (Lady Member)

1. You perform Kathak. Would you be okay if fusion dance forms are performed?


2. After I replied that as long as the philosophical core principles and techniques remain intact, innovation is acceptable, she again asked:
Would you still be okay with fusion?

3. You are a poet. Are poets observant individuals or social reformers?

4. Give one example to support your argument.

I cited Savitribai Phule and her literary work Bawankashi Subodh Ratnakar.

5. You have studied Sociology. Which concept do you find most useful?

I spoke about Social Facts.

Member 3

1. Taking a cue from the last discussion, did you take Sociology only from an exam perspective?

I explained my rationale.

2. You are an Electronics and Telecommunication engineer. Don’t you think an engineering degree certificate is merely a piece of paper?
(He was nodding in agreement in between.)

3. Why are there so many engineering colleges and high enrolment in states like Maharashtra and Karnataka, especially from a sociological point of view?

I spoke about the rise in aspirations and the preference for professional degrees.

4. He mentioned that in many Western countries, Electrical and Electronics syllabi are integrated, which is not the case in India.
Have you read the Electrical syllabus?

I replied in the negative.
He said, “No issues, it’s okay.”

5. This is a personality test—do you want us to know you more, or to test you?

I said that I would like them to know me more, and in that process, they would also test me.
(He smiled slightly.)

Member 4

1. You perform Lavani. It is a very energetic dance form. What does Lavani express?


2. What do you like about this dance form?


3. Suppose you help someone, but that person is neither grateful nor reciprocative. How would you express this through Lavani?

I said that I would first need to write a Lavani song to express that feeling, but in life, I do not let such experiences affect my helping nature—I continue doing my part.

He said, “Excellent, on that part.”


4. Describe Kanhoji Angre.
(Reference: Sindhudurg Fort)


5. Further discussion followed on the Marathas and his role in shipbuilding.


6. You are engaged in an exciting activity like cashew farming. Why, then, put in such hard work for civil services?( All of them exchanged smile among themselves)

Member 5

1. What is the percentage of protein in cashews?

2. What are the benefits of nuts like almonds and cashews?

3. What is a balanced diet?

4. Are you having a balanced diet these days?

I replied that I had one when I was at home, but since shifting to Delhi, the balance has been disturbed.

5. What is junk food?

6. What are its ill effects?

7. Should we ban all advertisements promoting junk food?

8. What can be done to control the spread of junk food?

9. Define culture.

10. Define Western culture. What are its traits, and why is it called so?

11. Tell me three women from
Maharashtra who inspire you.

I spoke about Savitribai Phule, Sindhutai Sapkal, and K. Majulaxmi (former Collector of my district).

The board member sitting next to him exclaimed, “All women?”
The member clarified that he was specifically asking about women.

12. You have a hobby of writing poems. Do you take time, or can you compose one on the spot?

I said that generally, I take time.

13. Can you write one now?

I asked if I could try writing a quote instead of a poem.
They agreed and allowed me to take my time using pen and paper.

While I was thinking, the Chairperson stood up to drink water. 
When I looked up, he waited and asked if I was ready.

I said, “Yes, sir.”

My quote was:

> “She was smiling because her strength was born out of the storms she survived.”

All members smiled and acknowledged it.
The Chairperson said that it was very quick.

Another member then said in Marathi:
“Jastich kadak zala ka interview?”
( May be he co related the term Storm with the interview )

I was surprised to hear Marathi from him, as I had assumed he was Punjabi (since he was wearing a turban). I asked him again to confirm it, and we smiled.

The Chairperson then said:
“It was great talking to you. You can leave now.”

I thanked them all and left.

It was a conversational interview.
All board member seemed genuinely interested in conversation.

1. One-to-one discussion with Anupam Jain Sir (Smartwork Labs)

He acted as a “calm in chaos,” helping me focus on what was truly needed and not get lost in clutter.

He hand-held me right from deciding the entries to be filled in the DAF.

We had detailed one-to-one discussions on each aspect of my DAF.

He guided me to think in the right direction, which significantly improved the quality and clarity of my answers.

Especially, discussions on my hobbies—particularly writing quotes—helped me a lot.

His trust in me strengthened my self-belief and helped me remain confident during the interview.

2. Pranay Agarwal Sir (IAS Gurukul)

Conducted detailed DAF-based questioning.
Very encouraging overall and helped boost confidence.

Helped me prepare DAF-based questions in a more structured and focused manner.

If you observe the pattern since the new Hon’ble Chairman took charge, one thing becomes quite evident: change has been the only constant.

-Changes in interview marks trends
-Evolving nature of Prelims question papers
-Introduction of provisional answer keys
-Aadhaar and face authentication
-Integration of the CSE application process
-New rules for selected candidates

Personally, i feel Mains examination may also come with some new flavour- more unconventional, unexpected, and pattern-breaking questions, much like what you witnessed in this year's Prelims.

If there is one thing UPSC has taught us recently, it is this: expect the unexpected.🤞🏻🤞🏻

Therefore, instead of spending endless hours discussing cut-offs, answer keys, and paper analysis, it may be wiser to shift your focus towards Mains preparation as early as possible.
